briefdescription.para: This Value has no known value yet.

detaileddescription.para: As a result, this implies the producing instruction is dead. Caution: We use this as the starting state in our local meet rules. In this usage, it's taken to mean "nothing known yet". Transition to any other state allowed.

briefdescription.para: This Value is an UndefValue constant or produces undef.

detaileddescription.para: Undefined values can be merged with constants (or single element constant ranges), assuming all uses of the result will be replaced. Transition allowed to the following states: constant constantrange_including_undef overdefined

briefdescription.para: This Value has a specific constant value.

detaileddescription.para: The constant cannot be undef. (For constant integers, constantrange is used instead. Integer typed constantexprs can appear as constant.) Note that the constant state can be reached by merging undef & constant states. Transition allowed to the following states: overdefined

briefdescription.para: This Value is known to not have the specified value.

detaileddescription.para: (For constant integers, constantrange is used instead. As above, integer typed constantexprs can appear here.) Transition allowed to the following states: overdefined

briefdescription.para: The Value falls within this range.

detaileddescription.para: (Used only for integer typed values.) Transition allowed to the following states: constantrange (new range must be a superset of the existing range) constantrange_including_undef overdefined

briefdescription.para: This Value falls within this range, but also may be undef.

detaileddescription.para: Merging it with other constant ranges results in constantrange_including_undef. Transition allowed to the following states: overdefined

briefdescription.para: We can not precisely model the dynamic values this value might take.

detaileddescription.para: No transitions are allowed after reaching overdefined.

briefdescription.para: Number of times a constant range has been extended with widening enabled.
The union either stores a pointer to a constant or a constant range, associated to the lattice element.

detaileddescription.para: We have to ensure that Range is initialized or destroyed when changing state to or from constantrange.

briefdescription.para: Destroy contents of lattice value, without destructing the object.
Returns true if this value is a constant range.

detaileddescription.para: Use UndefAllowed to exclude non-singleton constant ranges that may also be undef. Note that this function also returns true if the range may include undef, but only contains a single element. In that case, it can be replaced by a constant.

briefdescription.para: Returns the constant range for this value.

detaileddescription.para: Use UndefAllowed to exclude non-singleton constant ranges that may also be undef. Note that this function also returns a range if the range may include undef, but only contains a single element. In that case, it can be replaced by a constant.

briefdescription.para: Mark the object as constant range with NewR.

detaileddescription.para: If the object is already a constant range, nothing changes if the existing range is equal to NewR and the tag. Otherwise NewR must be a superset of the existing range or the object must be undef. The tag is set to constant_range_including_undef if either the existing value or the new range may include undef.

briefdescription.para: Updates this object to approximate both this object and RHS.

detaileddescription.para: Returns true if this object has been changed.

briefdescription.para: true, false or undef constants, or nullptr if the comparison cannot be evaluated.
Combine two sets of facts about the same value into a single set of facts.

detaileddescription.para:
Note that this method is not suitable for merging facts along different paths in a CFG; that's what the mergeIn function is for. This is for merging facts gathered about the same value at the same location through two independent means. Notes:
This method does not promise to return the most precise possible lattice value implied by A and B. It is allowed to return any lattice element which is at least as strong as either A or B (unless our facts conflict, see below).
Due to unreachable code, the intersection of two lattice values could be contradictory. If this happens, we return some valid lattice value so as not confuse the rest of LVI. Ideally, we'd always return Undefined, but we do not make this guarantee. TODO: This would be a useful enhancement.
